question: What does it mean that Christians are stewards?
answer: A steward is someone who looks after what belongs to another. Because "The earth is the LORD's, and all that fills it, the world and everyone who lives there" (Psalm 24:1), our money, time, abilities, bodies, relationships and even the gospel are placed in our hands by God. From the beginning humanity was told to work the garden "and take care of it" (Genesis 2:15): we are managers, not owners, and we manage before His face.

question: Do Christians have to tithe ten percent?
answer: In the Old Testament Israel gave a tenth: "All the tithe of the land belongs to the LORD" (Leviticus 27:30). In the New Testament all we are and all we have belongs to God, so it sets no fixed percentage. This book's view is that tithing and giving beyond it are good and worthy practices, but giving is guided by the Spirit and flows from grace and gratitude, not rules: "God loves a giver who gives gladly" (2 Corinthians 9:7).

question: What did Jesus teach in the parable of the talents?
answer: A master handed his property to his servants "according to what each could manage" (Matthew 25:15), and on his return praised the faithful ones with the same words: "Well done! You are a good and faithful servant. You proved faithful in small matters; I will put you in charge of great ones" (Matthew 25:21). Faithfulness, not the size of the gift, is what counts, and the servant who buried his silver out of fear is treated as a serious failure. Each of us "will have to give an account of ourselves" (Romans 14:12).
